newsitem.title: USA: Short interest hits record on NYSE, AMEX.
newsitem.headline: Short interest hits record on NYSE, AMEX.

text.p: Short interest rose to record highs on the New York and American stock exchanges in February, the exchanges said Friday, a sign some Wall Street analysts said was bullish for the market.
"Few bull markets have ended when scepticism is at such a high level," said Alan Ackerman, market strategist at Fahnestock & Co., commenting on the rise.
That is because short sales, an indication of the number of investors that expect stock prices to fall, can act as a cushion against market declines in many cases.
Investors who make short sales sell borrowed stock and hope to buy it back more cheaply, pocketing the difference. But this can force prices higher if the price of the "shorted" stock does not fall.

The New York Stock Exchange said short interest rose to 2.94 billion shares for the month ended Feb. 14 from 2.80 billion in mid-January, the exchange said. The previous high of 2.88 billion short shares was set in December.

The American Stock Exchange said short interest rose to 136.4 million shares, also as of Feb. 14, up nearly 14.3 million shares from 122.1 million as of mid-January. The previous record of 127.96 million was set in June 1996.
The exchanges report short interest on a monthly basis.

"Some people see short positions as a safety network," said Ackerman. "It would not be particularly surprising to see some of the short stocks do well" since the positions act as a cushion in many instances, he added.
